new_statements.quote: Como já postulado em outros trabalhos sobre o Yine (Piro-Manxineru) (cf. MATTESON, 1965; LIN, 1997; SEBASTIÁN, 2006; HANSON, 2010; COUTO, 2012; SILVA, 2013), o acento em Manxineru não é fonológico, pois não é contrastivo na língua. O aspecto mais consistente de tensão em Manxineru está na colocação de acento primário, que sempre ocorre na penúltima sílaba. Proeminências secundárias frequentemente ocorrem na primeira sílaba e em sílabas alternadas da esquerda para a direita, excetuando-se a sílaba adjacente ao acento primário.
new_statements.translation: As already posited in other works on Yine (Piro-Manxineru) (cf. Matteson 1965; Lin 1997; Sebastián 2006; Hanson 2010; Couto 2012; Silva 2013), stress in Manxineru is not phonological, since it is not contrastive in the language. The most consistent aspect of stress in Manxineru lies in the placement of primary stress, which always occurs on the penultimate syllable. Secondary prominences frequently occur on the first syllable and on alternating syllables from left to right, excepting the syllable adjacent to the primary stress.
new_statements.citation: Couto, Fábio Pereira. 2016. Conexões entre processos morfofonológicos e acento em Manxineru: a variedade Yine (família Aruák) falada no Brasil. Tese de Doutorado, Universidade de Brasília (orient. Ana Suelly A. C. Cabral). 368 pp.
new_statements.locator: Chapter XI, section 11.8.1 'O acento em Manxineru', p. 306 (page number printed in header); acoustic confirmation pp. 307-316; see also p. 124 (one main stress per word), pp. 112-114 (extrametricality), p. 231 (-ne/-te), pp. 276-280 (review of prior work)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (368 pp., text, no scanned) with extracted text. PDF page 306 carries printed header "306" and section heading "11.8.1 O ACENTO EM MANXINERU"; the quoted passage ("Como já postulado em outros trabalhos sobre o Yine (Piro-Manxineru) (cf. MATTESON, 1965; Linguistics Library, 1997; SEBASTIÁN, 2006; HANSON, 2010; COUTO, 2012; SILVA, 2013), o acento em Manxineru não é fonológico, pois não é contrastivo na língua. O aspecto mais consistente de tensão em Manxineru está na colocação de acento primário, que sempre ocorre na penúltima sílaba. Proeminências secundárias frequentemente ocorrem na primeira sílaba e em sílabas alternadas da esquerda para a direita, excetuando-se a sílaba adjacente…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress is predictable and non-contrastive: it falls on the penultimate syllable of the (phonological) word, regardless of how many prefixes/suffixes are added; when affixation changes the syllable count the stress shifts rightward so as to remain penultimate (e.g. [toˈlolo] 'sapo' ~ [toloˈlõne] 'sapos'). Couto's acoustic study (pp. 307-316) finds duration the most reliable correlate, with pitch and intensity less regular. Independent agreement from Silva 2013 p. 31 ('O acento em Manxinéri é previsível. A última sílaba da palavra é sempre de menor intensidade e a penúltima sempre a de intensidade mais forte' — syllabic trochee built right-to-left, weight-insensitive) and Silva 2008 p. 31 (same sentence).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Couto 2016 p. 306: secondary prominences frequently on the first syllable and on alternating syllables left-to-right, skipping the syllable adjacent to the primary stress; in sec. 9.1 (pp. 279-280) he relays Hanson 2010's finding for Yine that secondary stress is variable and does not always fall on the first syllable. Silva 2013 p. 31-32 analyses the foot as a weight-insensitive syllabic trochee built right-to-left, with degenerate feet allowed.
new_statements.exceptions: Couto 2016: 'salvo em questões extrassilábicas' (p. 306) — in trisyllabic words the absolutive suffix -tʃi is extrametrical, giving surface antepenultimate stress (pp. 112-114, e.g. [pi.hə̃ː.li.tʃi] 'olho'); the possessive mediators -ne/-te 'não afetam o acento do tema, mas criam um padrão de acento na antepenúltima sílaba' (p. 231); monosyllables carry stress. Couto 2012 p. 106 (earlier, impressionistic) allowed basic words with antepenultimate stress ([ˈwapə..] 'algodão'), later reinterpreted via extrametricality. Couto 2015 pp. 201-202: possessive concatenation shifts stress to the following syllable and lengthens its vowel; post-tonic final vowels reduce or delete under -tʃi.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the phonological word (ω), including long polysynthetic derived words; Couto 2016 p. 124 states there is only one main stress per word and per phonological phrase, and the intonation analysis (pp. 349-352) finds an F0 rise on the penultimate syllable of the phrase-final word followed by a fall. Data are from elicited words and short sentences of Mamoadate speakers, measured in Praat.
new_statements.identity_note: All five opened sources describe the Manxineru variety spoken in the Terra Indígena Mamoadate, southwestern Acre, Brazil (ISO mpd), i.e. Glottolog mach1268. Couto (2016) treats Manxineru as 'a variedade Yine (Macho-Piro) falada no Brasil' and cross-cites the Peruvian Yine/Piro descriptions (Matteson 1965, Lin 1997, Sebastián 2006, Hanson 2010 = yine1238), which report the same penultimate pattern; the quoted statement itself is first-hand for the Brazilian variety.

new_statements.quote: A última sílaba da palavra é sempre de menor intensidade e a penúltima é sempre a de intensidade mais forte, de modo que a intensidade não é fator distintivo entre as palavras. [p. 31] ... Embora na transcrição fonética tenha sido registrada a ocorrência de segmentos vocálicos longos, observa-se que essa ocorrência está associada facultativamente ao acento de intensidade, de modo que também não é distintiva. [p. 29]
new_statements.translation: The last syllable of the word is always the one of least intensity and the penultimate is always the one of greatest intensity, so that intensity is not a distinctive factor between words. [p. 31] ... Although long vocalic segments were recorded in the phonetic transcription, it is observed that their occurrence is optionally associated with intensity stress, so that it is likewise not distinctive. [p. 29]

new_statements.relation_note: Same placement as the catalog record (penultimate stress = penultimate) and as the existing Couto 2016 statement (stress non-contrastive, penultimate). Adds only that the acoustic cue named is intensity, that vowel length optionally accompanies the stressed syllable, and (in transcriptions) an initial secondary stress in four-syllable words, which Couto 2016 also reports.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary (intensity) stress falls on the penultimate syllable of every word; the final syllable is always the weakest; stress is predictable and therefore not contrastive. Vowel length is an optional concomitant of the stressed syllable, not phonemic.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not discussed in prose. The phonetic transcriptions mark a secondary stress on the initial syllable of four-syllable words, e.g. /katahiri/ [ˌkataˈhiːɾɪ] 'estrela' (p. 29), /patrapa/ [ˌpataˈlaːpa] 'galinha' (p. 31), consistent with an initial secondary prominence two syllables before the primary.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; the author notes that syllable structure and stress need more study once nominal and verbal paradigm data are available (p. 31). Two-syllable examples are transcribed with initial (= penultimate) stress, e.g. [ˈçetʃi] 'rede', [ˈhĩmhĩ] 'gordura'.
new_statements.identity_note: Silva 2008 describes the Manxinéri spoken in the Terra Indígena Mamoadate on the rio Iaco, southern Acre, Brazil (nine villages, Peri, Jatobá, Santa Tereza etc.), i.e. the Brazilian Machinere variety of Yine-Piro that glottocode mach1268 denotes; data from five native speakers recorded with Ana Suelly Cabral (p. 310 of the text). Not the Peruvian Yine (yine1238) described by Matteson 1965 and Hanson 2010.
